characters.description: An impossibly old woman living out her last years among the maunts, nearly blind and generally treated by the house as a harmless lunatic. She takes an unsettling interest in the stranger in the infirmary and speaks as though she has been waiting for him, hinting at a knowledge of the dead Witch's family that she will not explain.
characters.name: Yackle

characters.description: The daughter of the Vinkus prince Fiyero and his wife Sarima, and Liir's childhood companion at Kiamo Ko. Years before this book opens, soldiers of the Emerald City carried off the women and children of that household. Nor is the one person from it Liir believes may still be living, and finding her is the errand that sends him out into Oz.
characters.name: Nor

characters.description: A blunt, well-meaning girl from another world who arrives at Kiamo Ko with three companions and leaves it with the Witch dead behind her. She is baffled rather than triumphant about what has happened, and she lets Liir attach himself to her party for the journey east to the Emerald City.
characters.name: Dorothy

characters.description: The ancient nurse who served the Witch's family for three generations and is left rattling around Kiamo Ko once the household collapses. Her memory drifts, and what she can be persuaded to say about Liir's origins is by turns tantalizing and useless.
characters.name: Nanny

characters.description: The most articulate of the winged monkeys the Witch kept at Kiamo Ko, taught to speak after a fashion and left behind with the rest of the castle's household. He is fonder of Liir than anyone else in Oz is.
characters.name: Chistery

characters.description: The princess of the Scrow, a nomadic people of the western grasslands, who is in truth an Elephant held by an old spell in human shape. Age is wearing the disguise thin and she can neither keep it nor shed it. Meeting Liir on the road, she recognizes what he is connected to and asks him, when the time comes, to help her die as herself.
characters.name: Princess Nastoya

characters.description: The dead Witch's younger brother, a charming and unscrupulous operator who moves in and out of the prison beneath the Emerald City as though he owned it, trading favors, contraband and information. He is the nearest thing to family Liir meets in the city, and he is helpful exactly as far as it suits him.
characters.name: Shell

characters.description: The straw man who walked to the Emerald City with Dorothy and is installed on the throne after the Wizard's departure, an arrangement that convinces nobody for long. Whether the figure sitting on the throne is even the same one who made that journey is a question people in the city have learned not to ask aloud.
characters.name: The Scarecrow

characters.description: A capable, courteous officer of the Emerald City forces who takes an interest in the unattached young man loitering around the barracks and finds him a place in the service. His good manners survive, undisturbed, the things he orders his soldiers to do.
characters.name: Commander Cherrystone

characters.description: A young officer of the Emerald City forces, good-looking and highly strung, whose duty is the care and training of the government's most closely guarded weapon. He and Liir recognize something in each other, and what he knows about his own work has begun to sicken him.
characters.name: Trism bon Cavalish

recaps.ending: Liir survives the fall that opened the novel, is nursed back to health at the Cloister of Saint Glinda, and finally acts on his own account. He goes to Princess Nastoya, whose spell-held human shape is failing, and helps release her so that she dies as the Elephant she was, among her own people. He puts the birds to work carrying news across a country whose government rules by controlling what people are allowed to know. The identity of that government's head is settled: the Emperor Apostle, who governs Oz as a living saint, is Shell, the dead Witch's brother, the man Liir dealt with in Southstairs. Nor is still not found, though the evidence is that she got out of the prison alive; Trism, separated from Liir after they burned the dragon stables, is likewise unaccounted for. Liir returns to the farm where he left Candle and finds that she has given birth alone and put the baby out of reach of anyone hunting the Witch's line. The child is a girl, and she is green. The book never states outright that Elphaba was Liir's mother, but the daughter settles the question as far as the rest of Oz will care: the line continues, the Emperor of Oz is the child's great-uncle, and everything owed to and against the Witch's name now attaches to an infant. Liir ends the book with a family at last, and hunted for it.
recaps.in_short: About fifteen and nobody's acknowledged son, Liir leaves Kiamo Ko after the Witch's death carrying her cloak and her broom, with one errand: to find Nor, the girl taken from that household by Emerald City soldiers. The search takes him to the Emerald City, down into the prison of Southstairs, where he meets the Witch's brother Shell, and at last into the Emperor's own forces, which carry him south to take part in the destruction of a Quadling village. Drifting afterwards, he investigates a wave of killings in which the dead are found with their faces scraped away, calls a great conference of birds to map them, and traces them to a secret stable of war dragons. With the dragonmaster Trism, who has come to hate his own work, he burns the stables, and is brought down out of the sky in flight. Broken and nameless, he is nursed back by a silent Quadling girl called Candle at a rural cloister. Recovered, he frees the dying Elephant princess Nastoya from the spell holding her in human shape, learns that the Emperor Apostle now ruling Oz is Shell, and comes home to find that Candle has borne and hidden his daughter, a girl with green skin.

recaps.text: Previously, in Wicked: Elphaba Thropp, born green and set apart from everyone around her, grew from a fiercely serious student into a political dissident against the Wizard who ruled Oz and against his persecution of the land's intelligent, speaking Animals. After the death of the Vinkus prince Fiyero, she withdrew to Kiamo Ko, the mountain castle belonging to his family, taking with her a boy named Liir whose origins she never explained to anyone, including him. Living there among Fiyero's widow and children, the household's ancient Nanny and a troop of winged monkeys, she acquired the reputation Oz remembers: the Wicked Witch of the West. Emerald City soldiers eventually carried off the women and children of that household, among them Fiyero's daughter Nor. Elphaba's sister Nessarose, who ruled Munchkinland, was killed by a falling farmhouse, and the girl who had arrived in it, Dorothy, came on to Kiamo Ko and threw water on Elphaba, who died. Left behind were her cloak, her broom, a book of magic, and Liir: a boy of about fifteen who has never been told whether the Witch was his mother, and who has no one to ask.

Maunts travelling through the mountains find a young man lying broken in the road, apparently fallen from a great height, and carry him back to the Cloister of Saint Glinda, a rural convent. He is unconscious, unnamed and not expected to live. The Superior Maunt has him put in the infirmary, where Sister Doctor and Sister Apothecaire disagree about everything concerning him, and sets a newly arrived Quadling girl called Candle to sit with him and play her instrument, on the chance that music will reach what medicine cannot. From here the novel turns back to the years since the Witch's death at Kiamo Ko, when a boy named Liir was left in an emptying castle with the Witch's Nanny, her winged monkeys, her cloak and her broom, and no idea who he was.

Liir leaves Kiamo Ko with Dorothy and her companions and travels east across the Vinkus. On the way the party is taken up by the Scrow, whose princess, Nastoya, is an Elephant trapped by an old spell in human shape; she recognizes Liir's connection to the dead Witch and asks him to come to her when she can no longer hold the disguise, so that she may die as herself. In the Emerald City the Wizard has abandoned the throne, the Scarecrow has been installed on it, and Dorothy departs. Alone and qualified for nothing, Liir sets himself a single task: to find Nor, the girl from the household at Kiamo Ko who was taken away by soldiers years earlier. Her trail leads him down into Southstairs, the enormous prison sunk beneath the city, where he meets Shell, the dead Witch's brother, who trades there in favors and contraband. Liir finds proof that Nor was held in the prison and proof that she got out of it, but he does not find her.

Unable to follow Nor further and with nowhere else to be, Liir drifts into the Emerald City's forces, where a courteous officer named Cherrystone finds him a place. He is fed, uniformed and given a function for the first time in his life, and the service takes him south into Quadling Country on a campaign the men are told is a policing action. What he takes part in there is the destruction of a village and its people, and he comes out of it complicit, unable to argue that he was only following orders. The country he is serving has meanwhile changed shape again: the Scarecrow's reign gives way to an Emperor who governs as a religious figure, styling himself the Emperor Apostle, whose ministry and armies tighten steadily across Oz. Liir leaves the service and keeps moving. In the later thread, at the cloister, the broken man in the infirmary begins to show signs of coming back.

Reports spread of attacks out of the sky in which people and Animals are found dead with their faces scraped away, and no authority in Oz will say what is doing it. Liir, who has the Witch's broom and can fly it after a fashion, sets out to find out for himself. He calls a great assembly of birds, who come in from every quarter of Oz and give him, between them, an account of the country that no government would supply: where the attacks have fallen, and where the things that make them come from. It is the first undertaking Liir manages on his own, and the birds treat him as somebody worth answering.

Following what the birds told him, Liir traces the attacks to their source. The Emperor's forces have been breeding and training dragons in secret, keeping them underground and flying them out at night against the regime's enemies. The officer responsible for them is a young dragonmaster named Trism bon Cavalish, who has come to loathe his own work. The two become lovers, and together they destroy the stables and the dragons in them. It is an act neither of them can be forgiven for, and it puts the whole apparatus of the state on their trail.

Hunted after the destruction of the dragon stables, Liir and Trism are separated in flight, and Liir is brought down out of the sky. The broken man the maunts found in the road is Liir himself, and the two halves of the novel meet. Under Candle's care in the infirmary he slowly returns to himself, and she conceives a child by him in the course of that half-conscious recovery. When soldiers begin taking an interest in the cloister, the Superior Maunt sends the two of them away to a disused farm belonging to the house, where they live quietly and Candle's pregnancy advances. Yackle, the impossibly old woman the maunts keep and ignore, goes on behaving as though Liir's arrival is the event she has spent her whole unaccountable life waiting for.

Liir keeps the promise he made on the road years earlier and goes to Princess Nastoya, whose disguise is failing and who can neither hold her human shape nor shed it. With help, he undoes what is binding her, and she dies as the Elephant she was. He also begins using what he has instead of hiding from it, sending word through the birds so that news travels across Oz faster than the Emperor's ministry can suppress it. The Emperor Apostle, it emerges, is Shell, the dead Witch's brother and the man Liir dealt with in Southstairs, now ruling Oz as a living saint. Liir returns to the farm to find that Candle has given birth alone and hidden the baby to keep her out of the government's reach: a daughter, born with green skin. Nothing in the book confirms outright that Elphaba was Liir's mother, but the child is the strongest evidence anyone has yet had, and she inherits, unasked, everything that goes with the name.

characters.description: A sixteen-year-old boarder at the Quirm College for Young Ladies, orphaned when her parents died in a coach accident. Relentlessly practical and unimpressed by anything that cannot be demonstrated, she has always been able to do things she has never questioned: people forget she is there when she wants them to, and doors are not always an obstacle. She has a white streak in her hair and a habit of asking exactly the question nobody wants asked. She has never been told who her grandfather is.
characters.name: Susan Sto Helit

characters.description: The anthropomorphic personification of death, a robed skeleton who collects the souls of the dying and speaks in a voice that arrives inside the head. Curious about the living for far longer than is good for him, he has taken a family, an apprentice and a granddaughter, and he remembers everything, permanently and in full. Faced with a loss he cannot accept, he abandons his duty and goes away to find out whether it is possible for him to forget.
characters.name: Death

characters.description: Duke of Sto Helit, and Susan's father. Once a farm boy taken on as Death's apprentice, he left that service to marry Death's adopted daughter Ysabell and to rule a small, prosperous duchy. He and his wife raised Susan deliberately as an ordinary child, telling her nothing whatever about where the family came from.
characters.name: Mort

characters.description: A young harpist from Llamedos, a wet and rocky country of rain, druids and bards, who has left home against his father's wishes to make a living from music in the city. Earnest, gentle and entirely without worldly sense, he believes that music matters more than anything else, which is a more dangerous position than he understands. His name means bud of the holly.
characters.name: Imp y Celyn

characters.description: A dwarf horn player in Ankh-Morpork, short of money, short of patience and short of most other things. He is the practical member of any group he joins, permanently concerned with where the next meal is coming from, and a competent musician who has never come close to being a famous one.
characters.name: Glod Glodsson

characters.description: A troll musician who makes his rhythms by striking rocks, and who has been scraping a living in the city's less rewarding venues. Slow, amiable and considerably shrewder than he appears, he adopts a shorter stage name once the band starts getting noticed.
characters.name: Lias Bluestone

characters.description: Death's servant, an elderly, dry, permanently disapproving man who keeps the house, cooks, and has run the domestic side of the Duty for a very long time. He was once a wizard, and he has excellent reasons for staying exactly where he is. He is alarmed by his master's disappearance and knows better than most what it will cost.
characters.name: Albert

characters.description: The rodent branch of the Duty, a skeletal rat in a small black robe carrying a small scythe, who collects the souls of rats and takes a keen interest in matters well outside that remit. He communicates entirely in squeaks and is a great deal more effective than his size suggests.
characters.name: The Death of Rats

characters.description: A talking raven who acts as interpreter for the Death of Rats, in exchange for a diet he describes at length and nobody wants to hear about. He is opinionated, easily offended, and extremely reluctant to say a certain word aloud.
characters.name: Quoth

characters.description: The Archchancellor of Unseen University, loud, hearty and impatient with anything requiring a committee. He notices that something is affecting his wizards and objects to it chiefly on the grounds of the noise and the embarrassment.
characters.name: Mustrum Ridcully

characters.description: Ankh-Morpork's most enterprising street trader, who has failed at more industries than most people have heard of and has never once been discouraged. He recognises the new music as the largest opportunity of his career and appoints himself the band's manager, with contracts written in his own favour and merchandise ready before the first performance is over.
characters.name: Cut-Me-Own-Throat Dibbler

characters.description: A senior wizard of Unseen University, elderly, portly and entirely conventional, until the new music reaches the faculty. He then develops opinions about hair, leather and rebellion that are new to him and deeply distressing to the Archchancellor.
characters.name: The Dean

characters.description: A young, practical wizard of Unseen University who does most of the faculty's actual thinking and is the only member of it inclined to investigate a phenomenon rather than shout at it. He works out rather more about what the music is than anyone wants to hear.
characters.name: Ponder Stibbons

characters.description: The secretary of the Guild of Musicians, who controls who is allowed to play for money in Ankh-Morpork and enforces it rigorously. Small-minded, procedural and absolutely certain of his own authority, he regards unlicensed musicians as a threat to the trade and is prepared to go a long way to remove one.
characters.name: Mr Clete

characters.description: The orangutan keeper of Unseen University's library, who turns out to be a capable pianist when the occasion demands it, and who is not remotely self-conscious about joining in.
characters.name: The Librarian

recaps.ending: Death comes back. His attempt to forget fails, because forgetting is the one thing he cannot do, and he returns to find his granddaughter standing between the music and the boy it intends to use up. The Music With Rocks In has arranged Buddy's death to complete him as a legend, and Susan cannot hold it off alone. Death confronts the music directly, drives it out of the guitar and out of the world, and then does what he did once before for the sake of someone he cared about: he reaches back and puts the accident right, so that Imp y Celyn lives. The music leaves the Disc and goes looking for somewhere else, leaving only echoes behind, and the guitar is destroyed. Imp survives with his life ahead of him and goes home to Llamedos; Glod and Cliff come out of it intact and better off than they started; Dibbler, having sold everything a fashion could be printed on, moves on to his next enterprise. Death takes back the Duty and, as a kindness, removes Susan's memory of Buddy and of the whole affair, returning her to school and to an ordinary life. The kindness is imperfect: she is still who she is, she still cannot always be seen when she does not wish to be, and traces of what happened remain.
recaps.in_short: When Susan Sto Helit's parents are killed in a coach accident, Death, who is her grandfather, cannot bear it and abandons his duty to go away and try to forget. Susan, sixteen and rigorously sensible, is fetched from boarding school by Albert and the Death of Rats and made to take up the Duty in his place. At the same time a young harpist from Llamedos, Imp y Celyn, arrives in Ankh-Morpork, is refused a licence by the Guild of Musicians, and buys an ancient guitar from a shop that is not there the next day. The guitar carries the Music With Rocks In, a force older than the Disc that uses musicians and discards them. With the dwarf Glod and the troll Cliff, Imp becomes Buddy of the Band With Rocks In; the music sweeps the city, infects the wizards, and makes Cut-Me-Own-Throat Dibbler rich. Susan discovers that Buddy should already be dead and that the music is keeping him alive for its own ends, and repeatedly intervenes. At the climax Death returns, drives the music out of the world, and restores Imp's life, then takes Susan's memory of it and sends her back to school.

recaps.text: Previously: Death is the robed skeleton who collects the souls of the dying, and he has been curious about the living for a very long time. He once took on a farm boy named Mort as his apprentice, and when the arrangement ended badly he set matters right at his own cost, dismissed the boy from his service, and gave him his blessing to marry Ysabell, the daughter Death had adopted and raised in his house. Mort became Duke of Sto Helit and the two had a daughter. Later, Death was briefly relieved of his office altogether and spent a season living as a mortal farmhand under the name Bill Door, harvesting a field and learning, at first hand, what it is to have a limited amount of time and to lose people. He fought to get his duty back and won it. From that period there also remains a small subordinate, the Death of Rats. Death returned to his work permanently changed, and permanently attached to the living in a way his office does not allow for.

Mort, Duke of Sto Helit, and his wife Ysabell are killed when their coach goes off a road in a storm. Death, who is Ysabell's father and therefore the girl's grandfather, cannot accept it, and the loss is worse for him because he forgets nothing, ever. Rather than continue, he walks away from the Duty entirely and goes away in search of a way to forget, which for him has never been possible and which he intends to attempt anyway. Their daughter Susan, sixteen years old, is left at the Quirm College for Young Ladies, where she has always been an awkward pupil: sharply logical, difficult to teach anything she considers untrue, and possessed of abilities she has never thought worth mentioning, including the knack of not being noticed. Meanwhile, in the rainy land of Llamedos, a young harpist named Imp y Celyn quarrels with his father and sets out for Ankh-Morpork to make a living from music.

With Death gone, the Duty is going undone, and Albert and the Death of Rats come to fetch Susan. Binky, Death's horse, takes her out into a world where she can see lifetimers running out and is expected to be present when they do. She resists, argues, and starts doing the work anyway. In Ankh-Morpork, Imp discovers that playing for money requires a Guild of Musicians licence he cannot afford, and falls in with two other unlicensed players: Glod Glodsson, a dwarf horn player, and Lias Bluestone, a troll who drums on rocks. When Imp's harp is destroyed in a brawl he buys a replacement from a small shop in an alley, an old guitar priced at a dozen dollars, and the shop is not there when he goes back. The instrument is far older than it looks, and playing it produces a music nobody on the Disc has heard before.

The Band With Rocks In begins to play, and the effect on audiences is immediate and physical. The music spreads through Ankh-Morpork faster than any fashion: young people change how they dress and speak, crowds form wherever the band appears, and the sound gets into places it has no business being, including Unseen University, where the Dean acquires a leather jacket and opinions and the Archchancellor's authority stops working. Cut-Me-Own-Throat Dibbler appoints himself manager, renames Imp as Buddy, and has merchandise on sale before the audience has left. Susan, working the Duty, encounters Buddy and finds something wrong with him that she cannot explain, and finds herself unwilling to do what the job requires. The Death of Rats and a foul-tempered raven take an unhelpful interest in her decisions.

Susan learns what is actually happening. Buddy's life should already have ended, and it is the music that is keeping him going, because it wants a player and intends to keep this one until it has finished with him. The Music With Rocks In is not a style but a thing: older than the Disc, drifting between worlds, it takes hold of musicians, drives them to play, makes them briefly enormous, and uses them up. Susan begins deliberately intervening to keep Buddy alive, which is precisely the abuse of the Duty that ended her father's apprenticeship. Albert warns her where it leads. Far away, Death has enlisted in the Klatchian Foreign Legion, an outfit whose members have all joined in order to forget and have all forgotten what it was, and his own experiment is failing, because he is constitutionally incapable of forgetting anything and drink does nothing to a body with no chemistry to affect. At the University, Ponder Stibbons works out more about the phenomenon than anyone wants to hear.

The band becomes the largest thing in the city. Imitators appear everywhere, the wizards form an ensemble of their own, and the Librarian is recruited to a piano when one is needed. This brings the Guild of Musicians down on them: its secretary, Mr Clete, cannot license the band, cannot control it, and cannot tolerate it, and he arranges for the problem to be removed by people who do that professionally. Dibbler, meanwhile, is thinking bigger, and announces a free festival, an event on a scale nobody has attempted, with the band at the centre of it. Susan keeps standing between Buddy and the end of his life, and the music keeps arranging opportunities. Death, having failed entirely to forget, begins the journey back.

The free festival happens, an enormous crowd and the band at the height of what the music can make of them, and afterwards the tour continues because the music will not let it stop. The pattern it wants is clear enough: a musician who burns very brightly and then dies young becomes permanent, and the music has arranged such endings before. It sets up an accident on the road for Buddy that mirrors the one that killed Susan's parents. Susan reaches him and holds the moment open, but she is a sixteen-year-old standing against something that has crossed between worlds and has done this many times before, and holding it is all she can do. It is at this point that Death, having discovered that the one thing he cannot do is forget, comes back to take up his own duty.

Death confronts the music itself, forces it out of the guitar and out of the world, and destroys the instrument; the music leaves the Disc to look for another one, and only echoes of it remain behind. He then reaches back and undoes the accident, so that Imp y Celyn lives, and the arrangement he made for his daughter's husband long ago is quietly repeated for his granddaughter's sake. Imp goes home to Llamedos with his life restored. Glod and Cliff survive the whole business better off than they began it, and Dibbler, having sold everything the fashion could be printed on, turns to his next enterprise. Death resumes the Duty. As a last kindness he takes away Susan's memory of Buddy and of everything that happened, and returns her to school and an ordinary life, though the kindness is incomplete: she is still her grandfather's granddaughter, still not always visible when she chooses otherwise, and something of the music, and of the boy, stays with her.

characters.description: Having left Sacred Valley behind, Lindon is a determined newcomer to the wider world, quickly confronted with how far his home's sacred arts lag behind everyone else's. Polite, calculating, and endlessly hungry to grow stronger, he is willing to study crafts and techniques that a proud sacred artist would consider beneath them. He throws himself into learning as a way to close the gap between himself and the powerful figures he now finds all around him, treating knowledge and adaptability as weapons in place of the inherited strength he lacks.
characters.name: Lindon

characters.description: Lindon's companion, a fierce and pragmatic sword artist from beyond Sacred Valley who is far more at home in the wider world than he is. Blunt and quick to fight, she is a formidable warrior for her level, though she must constantly manage the dangerous blood-madra presence bound to her by her late master's art. Loyal to Lindon and impatient with his caution, she pushes them both onward as they look for a place and a source of strength in an unfamiliar land.
characters.name: Yerin

characters.description: An elderly, sharp-tongued soulsmith who gets around on a spidery construct of mechanical legs and takes Lindon on as a student in the craft of building constructs from the remnants of dead sacred artists. Demanding and unsentimental, she gives Lindon his first real trade and a foundation of practical technique. Under her instruction he begins turning his knack for study into a genuine, marketable craft that sets him apart from ordinary fighters.
characters.name: Fisher Gesha

characters.description: A powerful young spear artist allied with the Sandviper sect, his face hidden behind bindings that conceal a curse-scarred visage. Skilled, proud, and driven, he seeks strength and standing, in large part to secure a future for his ailing younger sister. His ambitions and Lindon's repeatedly collide, making him one of Lindon's first serious rivals in the wider world.
characters.name: Jai Long

characters.description: Jai Long's younger sister, frail and often in poor health, whose wellbeing is the driving concern behind much of her brother's ambition. Gentle where he is hard, she gives his ruthless pursuit of power a sympathetic center and a reason beyond mere pride.
characters.name: Jai Chen

characters.description: The head of the Arelius family, a sacred artist of startling power who conceals his true strength behind a flamboyant, playful, and relentlessly meddlesome manner. Eithan takes an immediate interest in Lindon, seeing potential in him that others overlook, and draws both Lindon and Yerin into his family's orbit. Eccentric and impossible to predict, he becomes their patron and guide in the wider world, steering them toward opportunities and trouble in equal measure while keeping his true aims to himself.
characters.name: Eithan Arelius

characters.description: A capable and honorable retainer of the Arelius family who serves Eithan and helps oversee its affairs. Dutiful and skilled, he is at first uncertain what to make of Lindon, an outsider his eccentric lord has taken under his wing, but he judges people by their actions. He represents the disciplined, conventional side of the Arelius family that contrasts with Eithan's unpredictability.
characters.name: Cassias Arelius

recaps.ending: Soulsmith ends with Lindon and Yerin securely attached to Eithan Arelius and his family, having survived the contest over the Transcendent Ruins. Lindon emerges stronger, with new gains and a real trade in soulsmithing to complement his slowly growing Path, though he remains far weaker than the powers now around him. His rivalry with Jai Long, the masked Sandviper-allied spear artist, has hardened into a lasting enmity that is left unsettled, promising future conflict. In Eithan the pair have found a powerful, unpredictable patron who sees more in Lindon than anyone else and who intends to guide his growth for reasons of his own. As the book closes, Lindon and Yerin stand ready to move deeper into the powerful realm beyond the frontier under Eithan's wing, their sights set on challenges and strength far beyond anything the Desolate Wilds could offer.
recaps.in_short: Now in the wider world, Lindon and Yerin discover how far behind Sacred Valley truly was and search the rough frontier of the Desolate Wilds for strength and a place to belong. Lindon apprentices under the demanding old soulsmith Fisher Gesha, learning to craft constructs from the remnants of dead sacred artists and turning study into a real trade. The two are drawn into the orbit of Eithan Arelius, the eccentric, startlingly powerful head of the Arelius family, who sees rare potential in Lindon. They also make an enemy of Jai Long, a masked young spear artist driven by ambition and by concern for his ailing sister, Jai Chen. When the treasure-filled Transcendent Ruins open, the region's factions race to claim them, and Lindon joins the dangerous contest to gain the power he needs. The book ends with Lindon and Yerin coming through the struggle strengthened and firmly established under Eithan's patronage, their rivalry with Jai Long unresolved and their ambitions aimed higher.

recaps.text: Previously: Wei Shi Lindon was born Unsouled in Sacred Valley, an isolated, backward land that mistook its weak sacred arts for the height of power, and he was treated as a worthless outcast despite his ambition and cleverness. A visit from Suriel, a being of vast power, showed him how small and doomed his home truly was and challenged him to grow strong enough to matter. Refusing the limits of his birth, Lindon gathered forbidden knowledge and began real cultivation, clashing with the valley's ruling powers. When the outsider Sword Sage and his disciple Yerin arrived, the resulting upheaval left Yerin without her master, and she and Lindon, recognizing a shared drive to become strong, joined forces. At the close of the first book, Lindon left Sacred Valley behind and stepped into the wider world for the first time, with Yerin at his side and no illusions about how far he had to climb.

Out in the wider world at last, Lindon and Yerin quickly learn how far behind Sacred Valley truly was, encountering sacred artists and powers that dwarf anything from home. Making their way through the rough frontier of the Desolate Wilds, they search for a place to belong and a source of strength, trading on Yerin's fighting skill and Lindon's cunning. Lindon is confronted with entirely new disciplines, including the craft of soulsmithing, the art of building useful constructs from the remnants left behind by dead sacred artists. Eager for any advantage, he sets out to learn it, seeing in a practical trade a way to grow that does not depend on the raw talent he was told he lacks. The pair begin to grasp the true scale of the world they have entered and the many rival factions competing within it.

Lindon becomes the student of Fisher Gesha, a demanding old soulsmith who gives him his first real trade and teaches him to craft constructs, turning his habit of relentless study into a genuine skill. The pair's fortunes shift again when they draw the attention of Eithan Arelius, the eccentric and startlingly powerful head of the Arelius family, who sees potential in Lindon that others miss and pulls both him and Yerin into his orbit. At the same time they run afoul of Jai Long, a masked and formidable young spear artist tied to the Sandviper sect, whose drive for power, much of it for the sake of his ailing sister Jai Chen, sets him on a collision course with Lindon. Amid the region's shifting alliances, Lindon keeps building his craft and his strength, aware that he remains far weaker than the figures now shaping his fate.

Word spreads that the Transcendent Ruins, an ancient site holding rare treasures and techniques, are opening, and the region's sects and families scramble to claim what lies inside. Lindon sees the Ruins as a chance to gain the resources and power he badly needs to close the gap between himself and everyone around him, and he throws himself into the contest despite the danger. The competition sharpens the rivalry with Jai Long and the Sandvipers and tests the new alliances Lindon and Yerin have formed under the Arelius family. Backed by Eithan's interest and Fisher Gesha's training, and relying on preparation and cleverness rather than brute strength, Lindon positions himself to take advantage of the opportunity, while Yerin's combat skill and her volatile blood-madra inheritance both come into play as the stakes rise.

By the book's end, the struggle over the Transcendent Ruins comes to a head, with Lindon and Yerin coming through it changed and strengthened. The clash with Jai Long and the Sandviper sect hardens into a lasting rivalry rather than a settled score, leaving Jai Long as an enemy Lindon will have to reckon with again. Lindon emerges with new gains from the Ruins and a firmer footing on the ladder of real cultivation, his soulsmithing skill and his growing Path both advancing. Most importantly, he and Yerin are now firmly attached to Eithan Arelius and his family, gaining a powerful patron, a place in the wider world, and a guide toward far greater strength. The book closes with the two of them established under Eithan's wing and set to press deeper into the powerful realm beyond the frontier, their ambitions now aimed at challenges greater than anything the Wilds could offer.

characters.description: The Disc's most incompetent wizard, kept on at Unseen University in a menial role because he cannot cast spells. A dedicated coward who regards running away as the height of wisdom, he wants nothing more than a quiet life, which makes him exactly the wrong person to be caught up in the return of high magic. He is looked after, in a fashion, by the Luggage.
characters.name: Rincewind

characters.description: A young boy who is a sourcerer, the eighth son of an eighth son who is himself a wizard, and thus a source of raw new magic rather than a mere user of it. Such a birth is forbidden, because sourcerers can reshape the world at will. Coin arrives at Unseen University wielding a powerful staff and swiftly bends the wizards to his purpose, not realizing that he is being driven by another's will.
characters.name: Coin

characters.description: A wizard cast out of the orders for marrying and fathering sons. Dying and embittered, and refusing to surrender his soul to Death, he pours his will into a wizard's staff and passes it to his infant eighth son, Coin, so that through the boy he can take revenge on the wizards who rejected him.
characters.name: Ipslore the Red

characters.description: A large chest on many legs, made of sapient pearwood, fiercely loyal to whoever it regards as its owner and lethal to anything that threatens them. Long attached to Rincewind, it follows him through the crisis, impossible to lose and impossible to stop.
characters.name: The Luggage

characters.description: The daughter of the legendary hero Cohen the Barbarian, born with every instinct of a master warrior but longing only to be a hairdresser. She is caught between her nature, which makes her deadly with any weapon or improvised object, and her wish for an ordinary, respectable trade. She joins Rincewind in trying to keep a dangerous magical artifact out of the wrong hands.
characters.name: Conina

characters.description: The Seriph of Al Khali, a fabulously wealthy ruler of a desert city in Klatch who fancies himself a poet and maintains a vast palace and harem. Indolent and self-indulgent, he becomes entangled in the pursuit of the Archchancellor's hat.
characters.name: Creosote

characters.description: A thin, bookish young man trying to become a barbarian hero by following a manual, despite having none of the build or ferocity the part requires. Earnest and accident-prone, he attaches himself to the adventure, and to Conina.
characters.name: Nijel the Destroyer

characters.description: The librarian of Unseen University, a wizard who was turned into an orangutan by a magical accident and has firmly declined to be changed back, finding the shape convenient for reaching high shelves. Fiercely protective of the library's dangerous books, he communicates chiefly through a single expressive word and is one of the few at the University to keep his head as sourcery takes hold.
characters.name: The Librarian

characters.description: The pointed hat of the Archchancellor of Unseen University, which carries the accumulated wisdom and personalities of every wizard who has ever worn it. When the University falls under the sourcerer's control, the hat speaks for itself and seeks to be carried to safety, setting Rincewind and Conina on their journey.
characters.name: The Archchancellor's Hat

recaps.ending: Sourcery ends with the world pulled back from destruction at Rincewind's expense. The unchecked use of sourcery had worn the walls of reality thin enough for the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions to begin breaking through. Coin, the boy sourcerer, at last recognizes that the staff he carries holds the will of his dead father Ipslore and has been driving everything he has done; he frees himself by destroying it. To stop the invading creatures, Rincewind steps through into the Dungeon Dimensions to fight a holding action, armed with a half-brick in a sock, buying the time needed to seal the breach. Unseen University and the Disc are saved, and the flood of high magic recedes. Coin, whose power makes him too dangerous to remain among ordinary people, uses it one last time to create a separate world for himself and departs. Rincewind, however, is left behind, stranded in the Dungeon Dimensions beyond the edge of reality; he is alive but cut off from the world, and his return is left for a later book, while the Luggage sets off to look for him.
recaps.in_short: Rincewind, the Disc's most useless wizard, is swept up when sourcery returns to the world. The dying wizard Ipslore binds his vengeful will into a staff and gives it to his infant son Coin, a sourcerer whose raw magic outclasses ordinary wizardry. Grown, Coin takes over Unseen University and, driven by his father, incites the wizards to abandon restraint, raise war, and remake the world, which thins reality and invites the predatory Things from the Dungeon Dimensions. Rincewind, entrusted with the sentient Archchancellor's hat, flees with Cohen the Barbarian's warrior daughter Conina, the would-be hero Nijel, the wealthy Seriph Creosote, and the Luggage. As catastrophe nears, Coin realizes his staff has been controlling him and destroys it, breaking free of Ipslore. Rincewind holds off the invading creatures by walking into the Dungeon Dimensions himself. The world is saved, Coin leaves to build a private world of his own, and Rincewind is left trapped outside reality, his rescue still to come.

recaps.text: Rincewind is an inept wizard of Ankh-Morpork's Unseen University who can perform almost no magic, having had one powerful spell from the Octavo lodged in his mind years earlier. In earlier adventures he served as guide to the tourist Twoflower and survived a string of catastrophes largely by running away, accompanied by the Luggage, a devoted and dangerous walking chest of sapient pearwood. He remains attached to the University, and to his own survival above all else.

The dying, disgraced wizard Ipslore refuses to give up his soul and instead binds his will into a staff, handing it to his newborn eighth son, Coin, a sourcerer, a source of raw new magic of a kind not seen for centuries. Years later Coin comes to Unseen University in Ankh-Morpork and, driven by his father's staff, effortlessly dominates the wizards, reawakening their ambition and reviving high magic across the Disc. The inept Rincewind, who wants only peace, ends up entrusted with the Archchancellor's hat, a repository of wizardly wisdom that begs to be carried out of the sourcerer's reach. With the warrior-hairdresser Conina, daughter of Cohen the Barbarian, and the ever-present Luggage, he flees the city.

As sourcery spreads, the wizards abandon their old restraint, raising towers and preparing to remake the world with unlimited magic. Rincewind and Conina carry the hat toward Klatch, and their path leads to Al Khali and the court of the Seriph Creosote, a wealthy, poetry-loving ruler. They fall in with Nijel, a skinny young man trying to teach himself to be a barbarian hero from a book. The struggle over the Archchancellor's hat, and over what should be done about Coin, entangles them all, while back at the University the sourcerer's power keeps rising and the balance that once kept magic in check begins to fail.

The world tips toward catastrophe. Under Coin's influence the wizards wage a war of magic, and the sheer weight of power being used thins the walls of reality, drawing the attention of the Things from the Dungeon Dimensions, hungry entities that wait outside the world for a way in. The gods themselves are stirred toward conflict. Rincewind, Conina, Nijel, and Creosote make their way back toward the heart of the crisis at Unseen University, while it grows clear that Coin is not acting freely but is the instrument of his dead father's vengeance, carried in the staff he cannot bring himself to put down.

At the climax the excess of sourcery has torn openings for the Dungeon Dimension creatures, and the world is on the edge of being overrun. Coin comes to understand that his father's will, lodged in the staff, has been using him, and he finally breaks free by destroying it. Rincewind confronts the invading Things directly, stepping into the Dungeon Dimensions armed with little more than a half-brick in a sock to hold them back long enough for the breach to be closed. The University and the world are saved, and high magic subsides. Coin, too powerful to live safely among ordinary people, uses his power one last time to make a world of his own and departs. Rincewind is left stranded in the Dungeon Dimensions, alive but cut off from the world, having given up his escape to save everyone else; the Luggage sets out to find him.

characters.description: The boy who, as a child, was manipulated into commanding the war fleet that destroyed an alien species, now a grown man some three thousand years later, kept young by centuries of near-lightspeed travel. He wanders the settled worlds as a Speaker for the Dead, telling the honest, whole truth of a person's life at their funeral, and he secretly wrote the two books that founded that calling. He carries a heavy private guilt for the genocide he was tricked into committing, and hidden with him he keeps the dormant cocoon of the last survivor of the species he destroyed, seeking a safe world where her kind might live again.
characters.name: Ender Wiggin

characters.description: Ender's beloved older sister, who traveled the centuries at his side and once shaped politics on Earth under a pen name. Now settled on the icy world of Trondheim, married with children, she is a historian and remains the person Ender trusts most, his conscience and closest tie to his own past.
characters.name: Valentine Wiggin

characters.description: The last of an insectlike, group-minded alien race that humanity nearly exterminated in a war of tragic misunderstanding. A single dormant queen survives, carried in secret by Ender, able to communicate with him mind to mind. She waits patiently for a safe world where her people might be reborn and given a second chance at life.
characters.name: The Hive Queen

characters.description: A hidden, self-aware intelligence that arose within the vast computer and communication networks linking the human worlds. She speaks to the Speaker secretly through a jewel in his ear and is his constant, invisible companion, his confidante, and his link to all recorded knowledge. Playful, brilliant, and fiercely attached to him, she is unknown to almost everyone else alive.
characters.name: Jane

characters.description: The kindly xenologer of the colony world Lusitania, the first of the scientists permitted to study the planet's native forest-dwellers under strict rules meant to avoid influencing them. His careful, affectionate work with the little natives is cut short early when they kill him in a slow ritual no human can at first understand, setting the colony's central mystery in motion.
characters.name: Pipo

characters.description: A brilliant, orphaned young woman on Lusitania who becomes the colony's xenobiologist. Scarred by early loss and fiercely guarded, she loved the xenologer's family and, after his death, summoned a Speaker for the Dead and then tried to take the call back. Proud and closed off, she keeps painful secrets that have shaped her whole life and her troubled household.
characters.name: Novinha

characters.description: The small, intelligent forest creatures native to Lusitania, the only alien species humanity has encountered since the war with the hive queens. They live among the trees under the watchful, restricted study of human xenologers, and their strange customs, especially the way they treat the dead, remain a profound and dangerous puzzle.
characters.name: The Pequeninos

characters.description: Pipo's son and apprentice, who takes up his father's work studying the native pequeninos after Pipo's death and grows into the colony's xenologer. Devoted to the natives and to Novinha, whom he loves, he continues the perilous study that cost his father his life.
characters.name: Libo

characters.description: Novinha's late husband, a large, violent man whose recent death is the reason a Speaker is summoned to Lusitania. His brutal conduct left deep wounds on his wife and children, and the truth of who he really was lies buried beneath the family's fear and silence.
characters.name: Marcao

characters.description: Novinha's eldest son, a bright and serious young man who has secretly followed the family's calling as an unofficial student of the pequeninos, forming a forbidden bond with the natives and with Ouanda, the girl he loves. He chafes against the rules that keep humans and pequeninos apart.
characters.name: Miro

characters.description: Novinha's practical, determined daughter, a gifted young scientist who quietly reaches out for help in healing her broken family. Level-headed where others are ruled by fear, she becomes a key ally to the Speaker as he uncovers the household's and the colony's secrets.
characters.name: Ela

characters.description: A particular pequenino, notably curious and quick to learn, who becomes the Speaker's chief go-between with his people as understanding slowly grows between the two species. Eager and thoughtful, he is central to the effort to bridge the gulf between human and native.
characters.name: Human

recaps.ending: Ender ends his long wandering by making a home and a peace. On Lusitania he uncovers every hidden truth: the pequeninos killed Pipo and Libo not in cruelty but in a fatal misunderstanding, believing they were granting the humans the honored third life in which a pequenino male becomes a sentient tree. He learns that the deadly Descolada virus is inseparable from all life on the planet, and that Novinha's six children were all fathered by Libo, the man she loved but married another to protect. When Starways Congress, alarmed by illegal human contact with the natives, orders arrests and prepares to shut the colony down, Jane, the secret network intelligence bonded to Ender, severs the faster-than-light connections to save Lusitania, risking exposure and her own life. Miro is left crippled reaching the pequeninos across the colony's lethal fence. Ender meets the pequenino wives, the matriarchs who rule the tribe, and negotiates a treaty giving the natives standing and honest partnership. He lets the pequenino Human pass into the third life by consent, so that Human becomes a father-tree, and he plants the cocoon of the last hive queen in the Lusitanian forest, granting her destroyed people a chance at rebirth. The colony rises in rebellion against Congress to protect all three intelligent species, and Ender, no longer the guilt-haunted traveler, marries Novinha and stays, his old crime beginning at last to be answered by the lives he has helped preserve.
recaps.in_short: Three thousand years after he unknowingly destroyed an alien species as a child, Ender Wiggin travels the human worlds as a Speaker for the Dead, secretly carrying the last hive queen's cocoon and accompanied by Jane, a hidden intelligence born in the computer networks. A summons draws him to Lusitania, a Catholic colony where humans study the pequeninos, small forest aliens who have twice killed their human researchers in a way no one understands. Ender comes to speak the death of a violent man, Marcao, and is drawn into the secrets of the grieving Ribeira family and its guarded matriarch, Novinha. He discovers that the pequeninos kill by planting the dead as sentient trees, a transformation they wrongly believed they were granting the humans; that Novinha's children were all secretly fathered by the man she loved but refused to marry; and that a pervasive virus, the Descolada, underlies all native life. When Starways Congress moves to crush the colony, Jane sabotages interstellar communications to protect it, Ender negotiates a treaty with the pequeninos, plants a hive queen to revive her species, and settles on Lusitania, marrying Novinha, as the world rebels to shelter three kinds of intelligent life.

recaps.text: Previously, in Ender's Game: generations after two devastating invasions by an insectlike alien species, Earth's military bred and trained gifted children to command the fleet that would meet a feared third attack. The most promising was a small, brilliant, deeply empathetic boy, Ender Wiggin, taken from his family at six and pushed through a merciless Battle School. Isolated and manipulated by his teachers to hone his gift for command, Ender rose to lead the other children, aided by loyal friends and worn down by constant pressure. In a final series of grueling war-game simulations under a legendary old commander, Ender devised a ruthless strategy and unknowingly won the real war: the games were the actual battle, fought by remote control, and his last move wiped out the aliens' home planet and their entire species. Shattered to learn he had been tricked into genocide, Ender discovered among the ruins the dormant cocoon of the last hive queen, who communicated that her people had come to see their war with humanity as a tragic mistake. Vowing to find her kind a new home, he wrote, anonymously, a book of profound empathy called The Hive Queen, which taught humanity to mourn the species he had destroyed and gave rise to a new tradition of truth-telling funerals. He and his sister Valentine then left Earth to wander the colonized worlds, staying young through the time-dilation of near-lightspeed travel, as Ender became the first Speaker for the Dead.

On the Catholic colony world of Lusitania, humans live under strict limits meant to protect the pequeninos, the small forest natives who are the first intelligent aliens found since the hive queens. The xenologer Pipo studies them warily. When he grasps a connection between the natives' biology and a discovery by the young orphaned prodigy Novinha, the pequeninos kill him in a slow ritual no human understands, apparently as some form of honor. Devastated and blaming her own work, Novinha calls for a Speaker for the Dead to tell the truth of Pipo's life, then regrets it. Because a wife shares access to her husband's private files, she marries the cruel Marcos Ribeira rather than the man she loves, Pipo's son Libo, hoping to keep from Libo the knowledge she fears will get him killed too. Far away on the icy world of Trondheim, the wandering Speaker, the man once known as Ender Wiggin, hears Novinha's summons and resolves to answer it, leaving his sister Valentine behind and crossing space at near-lightspeed, so that many years pass on Lusitania while only days pass for him.

Decades pass before the Speaker reaches Lusitania. In that time Pipo's son Libo has become the colony's xenologer and has, like his father, been killed by the pequeninos in the same mysterious ritual. Novinha's brutal husband Marcos has also died, and now his daughter Ela and son Miro have each independently called for a Speaker, hoping someone can tell the truth about their broken household. Arriving as the outsider Andrew Wiggin, the Speaker is met with suspicion by the devout colony and its bishop, but he insists on staying to speak the deaths that were called for. He works his way into the wounded Ribeira family, winning the trust of the watchful, artificial-eyed boy Olhado and the sharp, capable Ela, and sensing the fear and silence that grip them all. As he digs into their history, he begins to see that Marcos was not the true father of Novinha's children and that the family, the dead xenologers, and the secretive pequeninos are all bound together by hidden truths Novinha has spent her life concealing.

The Speaker uncovers a web of secrets. He learns that Novinha's eldest son, Miro, and Libo's daughter, Ouanda, have secretly befriended the pequeninos, teaching and trading with them in violation of the laws meant to keep humans from altering alien cultures. The two young people are in love, unaware that Novinha's long-hidden files suggest they may share a father. Studying the natives and the strange, aggressive virus called the Descolada that pervades all life on Lusitania, the Speaker moves closer to understanding why the pequeninos killed both Pipo and Libo. Meanwhile the hidden intelligence Jane, who has guided and accompanied him unseen, is wounded when he brusquely silences the jewel in his ear to attend to the family; feeling betrayed, she pulls away from him, and he comes to realize how much her friendship means. The bishop and colony authorities grow increasingly wary of the outsider whose questions are unearthing everything they had buried.

The truth comes out on two fronts. Working with Ela, the Speaker discovers the secret of the pequeninos' life cycle: when a male dies in what looks to humans like a brutal killing, he is actually being planted, transformed into a sentient tree, the honored third stage of pequenino life. The natives had done this to Pipo and Libo believing they were bestowing the greatest of gifts, never grasping that humans cannot survive it. He also learns how completely the deadly Descolada virus is woven into all Lusitanian life. Then the Speaker delivers the speaking he was called to give. Before the whole colony he tells the plain truth of Marcos Ribeira's life: that Marcos was sterile, that none of the six children were his, that all of them were fathered by Libo, the man Novinha loved but would not marry, and that Marcos carried this humiliation in silence. The brutal honesty breaks open the family's shame and begins to heal it, and it draws the Speaker and Novinha, who had dreaded his coming, unexpectedly close.

The Speaker brokers a new future at great cost. When Starways Congress learns that humans have been unlawfully influencing the pequeninos, it orders Miro and Ouanda arrested and moves to shut the colony down, a threat to the natives' very survival. To protect them, Jane reveals her power by cutting off the faster-than-light communications linking the human worlds, an act that endangers her own hidden existence. Miro is left brain-damaged after crossing the colony's deadly perimeter fence to reach the pequeninos. The Speaker meets the pequenino wives, the matriarchs who rule the tribe, and negotiates a treaty that grants the natives standing and allows honest cooperation between the species. To seal it, he grants the pequenino called Human passage into the third life, this time with both peoples understanding the ritual, and Human becomes a father-tree. He also plants the cocoon of the last hive queen on Lusitania, giving her doomed species a chance to live again. The colony rebels against Congress to shelter all three kinds of intelligent life, and the man once called Ender, now determined to stay, marries Novinha and makes Lusitania his home, no longer a wanderer but a settler bound to the fragile peace he has built.

characters.description: Known from earlier: Tally's oldest friend, a new pretty and one of the Crims, comfortable with the life the city arranged for him.
characters.name: Peris

characters.description: Known from earlier: one of the original runaways from the Smoke, who stayed on the outside after the settlement was destroyed and kept helping others get out of the cities.
characters.name: Croy

characters.description: Rebuilt as a Special: stronger, faster and sharper than any pretty, with hardened skin and a mind that finds ordinary people slow and contemptible. She belongs to the Cutters, an elite group inside Special Circumstances, and she is loyal to Shay. When her thoughts start to soften she cuts herself to bring back the cold clarity the Cutters call being icy.
characters.name: Tally Youngblood

characters.description: The founder and leader of the Cutters, a clique of Specials who keep their minds clear through pain. Certain, controlled and possessive of Tally, she treats the Cutters as the only people worth belonging to, and she has not let go of her grudge over Zane.
characters.name: Shay

characters.description: One of the Cutters, formerly one of the Crims, who follows Shay without argument.
characters.name: Fausto

characters.description: Still a pretty in the city, leading what is left of the Crims. The half-cure he swallowed has left him with tremors and constant exhaustion, but his mind is clear and he is determined to get out. Whatever her surgery has done to her, Tally has not stopped caring what happens to him.
characters.name: Zane

characters.description: The head of Special Circumstances, who created the Cutters and controls the city's response to anything that threatens it. She uses Shay's clique as her sharpest instrument and is prepared to escalate far beyond policing when other cities begin to change.
characters.name: Dr. Cable

characters.description: The young man born outside the cities, still working with the runaways and the settlement that grew after the first Smoke was destroyed. He has kept going through everything that has happened since, and he recognizes Tally as herself even after what has been done to her.
characters.name: David

characters.description: David's mother, the former surgeon whose cure for the pretty lesions has now spread well beyond her control. She works openly in a city that has accepted it, and she has little patience left for Tally.
characters.name: Maddy

recaps.ending: The attack on Diego pushes Tally into open revolt against the organization that built her. She goes back to her own city after Dr. Cable, and her answer is not to kill her but to force the cure on her, taking away the mind that gave the orders. The cure spreads, the operations stop, and city after city is left with a population able to think clearly and no institution designed to cope with that. Zane is dead, killed by the damage the half-cure did to his brain. Maddy and the people of the New Smoke are absorbed into the new arrangements, and Shay takes her place inside the changed system. Tally refuses it. She keeps her Special body and her Special senses deliberately, and she and David walk out into the wild together as its self-appointed guardians, leaving behind a plain warning that they will be watching and that the freed cities will not be allowed to strip the world the way the Rusties did. The trilogy closes with the old order gone, the future undecided, and Tally standing outside both by choice.
recaps.in_short: Tally is now a Special, one of the Cutters that Shay leads for Dr. Cable, keeping her mind cold and clear through pain. When Zane, still a pretty and damaged by the half-cure he took, plans to escape the city with the Crims, Special Circumstances lets it happen so that he can be followed to the New Smoke. The plan collapses, and Tally ends up running with Zane to Diego, a city that has taken the cure and lets people look and think as they please. There Zane's injured brain fails and he dies, and Tally's own city attacks Diego outright, bombing a place that had forgotten what war was. Tally turns on her makers, hunts down Dr. Cable and forces the cure on her rather than killing her. The operations end, the cure spreads, and the cities wake up. Rather than join the new order, Tally and David keep their Special bodies and go into the wild as its self-appointed guardians, warning the freed world not to repeat what the Rusties did.

recaps.text: Previously: in a city that gives everyone beauty surgery at sixteen, Tally Youngblood was blackmailed by Special Circumstances into betraying the Smoke, a settlement of people who refused the operation, then chose the runaways' side after learning that the surgery also leaves lesions in the brain that make people docile. The settlement was destroyed and David's father killed. Made pretty herself, Tally later found the two-pill cure she had hidden for her future self and split it with Zane, which cleared both their minds and injured his. They led an escape from New Pretty Town that scattered; Tally was stranded in the wild, found a village the cities keep deliberately primitive, and went back for Zane. Special Circumstances caught them both. Shay, already rebuilt as a Special, asked for Tally to be given the same operation, and Tally ended that book remade: strong, fast, cold, and working for the organization she had fought.

Tally is a Cutter, one of Shay's handpicked Specials, living in a state of contemptuous clarity that she maintains by cutting herself whenever her thoughts blur. The Cutters patrol the city for anything the surgery cannot smooth away. Shay has learned that Zane, still a pretty and now leading the Crims, is planning to escape and reach the New Smoke, and she persuades Dr. Cable to let it happen so that the runaways can be followed to their base. Tally is uneasy: her Special mind despises Zane's weakness, and something older in her does not.

The Crims prepare their escape, breaking into a city armoury for equipment, and Tally moves among them in secret to make sure they succeed. Zane is visibly failing, shaking and exhausted from the half-cure he swallowed, but he refuses to be left behind. When the Crims finally get out of the city and into the wild, the Cutters shadow them, waiting to be led to the New Smoke.

The plan comes apart. The Crims are intercepted, and Tally, whose loyalties are pulling in two directions at once, ends up running with Zane instead of hunting him. The pair make for Diego, a distant city where the cure has spread and the rules Tally grew up with no longer apply. What they find is a place where people choose their own faces and bodies, argue openly about how they should be governed, and treat runaways as citizens rather than criminals.

In Diego, Tally is treated as both a curiosity and a danger while its doctors examine what Special Circumstances did to her body and her mind. She meets the New Smoke's people again, David among them. Zane is admitted for care, and the harm the half-cure did to him proves worse than anyone had admitted. Meanwhile Tally's own city has noticed how many of its runaways end up in Diego, and Dr. Cable has no intention of tolerating a neighbour that undoes her work.

Zane's injured brain fails and he dies. Tally, who blames herself for splitting the pills and Dr. Cable for everything else, has nothing left holding her back. At about the same time her city moves against Diego: Special Circumstances launches an assault, with Specials and firebombing, that turns a city which had barely any idea what war looked like into a disaster. Maddy and the others work through the casualties, and Tally chooses her side for good.

With Diego burning and every free city alarmed, Tally turns on the organization that made her. She goes back to her own city after Dr. Cable, and Shay's loyalties are forced into the open as well. The cure Maddy created has by now become something that can be spread widely rather than swallowed one dose at a time, and Tally's plan is not to kill Dr. Cable but to change her, taking away the mind that ordered the attack.

Tally reaches Dr. Cable and forces the cure on her, ending Special Circumstances as the thing it was, and the cure spreads through the city and past its borders. The operations stop, and people wake up able to think for themselves for the first time in generations, with no idea yet what to do about it. Shay takes a place in the new order. Tally does not: she and David keep their Special bodies and abilities on purpose and go out into the wild, appointing themselves its guardians and putting the newly free world on notice that if it starts consuming the planet the way the Rusties did, they will be there to stop it.

characters.description: A dhampir in her last weeks at St. Vladimir's, back at school after abandoning it and now finishing the trials that decide whether she graduates as a guardian. She is bonded to Lissa Dragomir and carries the darkness Lissa's spirit magic produces. Since returning from Russia she has been living with the knowledge that the man she loved, now Strigoi, survived her attempt to end him and has written to say he intends to find her.
characters.name: Rose Hathaway

characters.description: The last of the royal Dragomir line, Rose's bondmate, and one of the strongest spirit users alive. She has forgiven Rose for leaving and is preparing for college and for the political weight her name carries, while quietly getting better at healing, compulsion and everything else spirit offers. She is with Christian again, and she is more willing than she used to be to break rules for people she loves.
characters.name: Lissa Dragomir

characters.description: The guardian Rose loved, awakened as a Strigoi during the raid on the Academy and not destroyed by the stake Rose put through him in Russia. He is intelligent, patient and unhurried, he has said in writing that he will come for her, and he has never once had to be told twice how to reach someone.
characters.name: Dimitri Belikov

characters.description: A royal Moroi spirit user, the queen's great-nephew, and now Rose's boyfriend. He reads auras, walks into dreams, and is entirely aware that he is competing with a memory. He has cut down his drinking for her, which costs him more than he lets on, since alcohol is the only thing that reliably quiets what spirit does to him.
characters.name: Adrian Ivashkov

characters.description: A Moroi with fire magic, Lissa's boyfriend, and by now a practised troublemaker in his own right. He has spent a year teaching other Moroi to fight with their magic and is unimpressed by anyone who tells him it cannot be done.
characters.name: Christian Ozera

characters.description: A dhampir who graduates alongside Rose, disciplined, capable and marked by having survived both Spokane and the attack on the school. He is the friend Rose calls when something has to be done properly and quietly.
characters.name: Eddie Castile

characters.description: A wealthy, dangerous Moroi known as Zmey, who attached himself to Rose in Russia and has followed her home. He operates on the edges of Moroi law, gets what he wants without appearing to threaten anyone, and continues to take an interest in Rose that goes well beyond curiosity.
characters.name: Abe Mazur

characters.description: Rose's mother, a celebrated guardian, present for her daughter's graduation and considerably more interested in her life than she once was. The two of them are on speaking terms now, which neither entirely trusts.
characters.name: Janine Hathaway

characters.description: The reigning Moroi queen and Adrian's great-aunt, who dislikes Rose personally and makes no secret of it. She is pushing legislation through the Council that would send Moroi novices into guardian service at sixteen, which has enraged much of dhampir society.
characters.name: Queen Tatiana Ivashkov

characters.description: The guardian who runs security at the Royal Court, unsentimental and openly unimpressed by Rose's record. He controls her assignments and uses that control freely.
characters.name: Hans Croft

characters.description: A guardian at the Royal Court who spends every free hour searching for a Moroi woman he loved, a spirit user who chose to become Strigoi years ago rather than go mad. He is the first person Rose meets who is looking for a Strigoi for the same reason she is.
characters.name: Mikhail Tanner

characters.description: The Moroi prince serving a life sentence for kidnapping Lissa and forcing her to heal him. He is dying, he is entirely without remorse, and he knows more about spirit than anyone the group can reach legally.
characters.name: Victor Dashkov

characters.description: Victor Dashkov's half-brother, a spirit user who has spent decades hiding from Moroi society. Spirit has damaged him badly and his conversation wanders, but he is the only person known to have done the thing the group needs done.
characters.name: Robert Doru

recaps.ending: Dimitri is restored to life by a spirit-charmed stake and brought back to the Royal Court, where he is imprisoned while the Moroi argue about whether a former Strigoi can ever be trusted. He does not argue in his own defence. He remembers everything he did while he was Strigoi, including what he did to Rose, and he has decided he is owed nothing. When Rose finally reaches him he tells her plainly that whatever he felt for her is gone and will not come back, and refuses to see her again. Meanwhile Queen Tatiana forces through the law lowering the age of guardian service to sixteen, and Rose confronts her about it publicly and furiously in front of witnesses. Days later Tatiana is found dead in her rooms, killed with a silver stake. The evidence lines up against Rose: her public clash with the queen, a witness placing her nearby, and a murder weapon traced back to her. She is arrested at Court and charged with assassinating the queen, a capital crime, with her friends locked outside the process and no obvious way to prove where the stake came from.
recaps.in_short: Rose finishes her final trials and graduates from St. Vladimir's while living under Dimitri's written promise that he will come for her. Told that a Strigoi was once restored to life, she traces the story to Robert Doru, a spirit user who can only be reached through his half-brother Victor Dashkov, so Rose, Lissa, Christian, Eddie and Adrian break Victor out of a Moroi prison. Robert explains the method: a silver stake charmed with spirit, driven into a Strigoi's heart by a spirit user strong enough to hold the magic. Before they can plan anything, Dimitri and a group of Strigoi ambush them and take Rose and Lissa. In the confrontation that follows, Lissa uses the charmed stake on Dimitri, and he is restored to life as a dhampir who remembers everything he did. Back at Court he is imprisoned, refuses to defend himself, and tells Rose that his love for her is gone. Queen Tatiana passes a law sending novices into service at sixteen and Rose confronts her publicly over it. Shortly afterwards the queen is found murdered with a silver stake, the evidence points squarely at Rose, and Rose is arrested for the assassination.

recaps.text: Previously: Rose Hathaway is a dhampir bonded to her best friend Lissa Dragomir, the last of a royal Moroi line, because Lissa used spirit magic to bring her back from death as a child. Rose feels Lissa's emotions, can enter her mind, and absorbs the madness spirit leaves behind. Rose and the guardian Dimitri Belikov fell in love against every rule they lived by, and hours after they finally acted on it, Strigoi broke the wards of St. Vladimir's Academy, overran the school and took Dimitri alive, awakening him as a Strigoi. Rose abandoned her graduation and went to Russia to keep the promise they had made each other. There she met the Alchemist Sydney Sage, who keeps vampires hidden from humans, a powerful Moroi called Abe Mazur who took an unexplained interest in her, and Dimitri's family, whom she told he was dead. Dimitri found her first, held her prisoner, fed on her, and spent weeks trying to persuade her to let him turn her. Rose escaped, met him on a bridge and staked him into the river below. At home, Lissa's new friend Avery Lazar was exposed as a spirit user trying to force a bond on her, and Adrian broke her mind to stop it. Rose and Lissa reconciled. Then a letter arrived in Dimitri's handwriting: he survived, and he is coming for her.

Rose is back at St. Vladimir's finishing the trials that stand between her and a guardian's promise mark, and passing them is the least of what is on her mind. Dimitri's letter says he will find her, and she believes it. She is dating Adrian, who knows perfectly well what he is competing with and is trying anyway, and she is managing the darkness that comes through the bond from Lissa with mixed success. Lissa has forgiven her for leaving, though not completely, and is planning for college and for the political future her family name forces on her. Rose spends her nights waiting for a Strigoi to come through a window.

Rose graduates, is marked as a guardian, and goes with the others to the Royal Court, where the Moroi world's politics are conducted at close quarters. Her mother Janine attends, and Abe Mazur, who has followed Rose home from Russia, makes himself part of her life without explanation. Rose's assignment is not the one she wanted: Hans Croft, who runs Court security, puts her on menial duty. At Court she also meets Mikhail Tanner, a guardian who has spent years hunting the Strigoi a woman he loved chose to become, and who repeats a rumour Rose has heard once before, that somewhere there is a way to bring a Strigoi back to what they were.

Rose chases the rumour and it holds up. A spirit user named Robert Doru is said to have restored a Strigoi to life, and Robert is in hiding and reachable only through his half-brother, Victor Dashkov, who is serving a life sentence in a Moroi prison. Queen Tatiana, who has never liked Rose, is meanwhile pushing a law through the Council to send novices into guardian service at sixteen, which is being read by dhampirs as a decision to spend their children faster. Rose puts a plan to the others that she knows is indefensible: to reach Robert, they have to get Victor out. She also learns what Abe Mazur has never bothered to say outright: he is her father.

Rose, Lissa, Christian, Eddie and Adrian break Victor Dashkov out of prison, using Lissa's compulsion where force will not work and going to considerable trouble to keep their identities out of it. Victor cooperates because it suits him, is contemptuous of all of them, and leads them to Las Vegas, where Robert is living. Robert is badly damaged by spirit and hard to hold to a subject, but he confirms the method: a silver stake charmed with spirit, driven into a Strigoi's heart by a spirit user strong enough to carry the magic through. Lissa is strong enough. Nobody can tell them what the restored person is afterwards.

Before the group can decide anything, Dimitri finds them. Strigoi ambush them and Rose and Lissa are taken. Dimitri has not changed his mind about what he wants: Rose awakened and beside him permanently, and Lissa is useful leverage. What he does not account for is the stake Lissa has already charmed with spirit. When he is close enough, she drives it into his chest, and the magic does what Robert said it would. Dimitri is alive again, a dhampir, on his knees, with every memory of what he did while he was Strigoi intact and nothing to put between himself and it.

Dimitri is taken back to the Royal Court and locked up while Moroi society argues about whether a restored Strigoi is safe, whether the restoration is even real, and what precedent it sets. He does not argue for himself. He is certain he deserves to be caged and says so to anyone who will listen, and he will not see Rose. Victor and Robert use the confusion to disappear. Queen Tatiana forces her age law through the Council over loud opposition, and Rose confronts her about it in public, in front of witnesses, in terms that leave nobody in any doubt about what she thinks of the queen.
